photographic_art.label: Antarctic photographic art
facts: The exhibition is an immersive photographic journey through Antarctica, built with photographs, light, and a room-by-room emotional sequence.
The work Purple Dawn can look almost three-dimensional, but its unusual color comes from real Antarctic light rather than computer graphics.
The Sun and Ice triptych uses three photographs together to turn Antarctic light and ice into one visual story.

photographer.label: photographer Sergey Potetyunin
facts: Sergey Potetyunin is the photographer, author, and traveller behind the exhibition.
After a spinal injury and years of pain, Sergey rebuilt his life through yoga and martial arts before travelling to the Himalayas and Antarctica.
Describe Sergey's talent through patience, composition, natural light, and emotional observation; never use unsupported rankings or superlatives.

expedition_story.label: Antarctic expedition story
facts: The Antarctic expedition began in February 2024 in Ushuaia and continued across the Drake Passage.
The Drake Passage is presented as a psychological border before entering another world.
The first iceberg at sunrise is the emotional moment when one world seems to end and another begins.

installation.label: exhibition installations
facts: The gentoo penguin nest installation shows a father, a down-covered chick, and a mother away finding food; its theme is tenderness together with vulnerability.
A porthole installation opens onto a penguin family and a view of the bay.
The photo zone places visitors visually on board a liner near Antarctica.
